annotations.annotation_text: Introduction of Peter Riviera, a sociopathic holographic performer and sadomasochist whose subdermal optic implants project living hallucinations, recruited to exploit 3Jane's aesthetic tastes.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 56.

annotations.target_phrase: The matrix has its roots in primitive arcade games
annotations.annotation_text: The historical lineage connecting 1970s and 1980s coin-op video arcade games directly to military flight simulators and neural cyberspace navigation.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 56.

annotations.target_phrase: Cyberspace. A consensual hallucination experienced daily by billions of legitimate operators
annotations.annotation_text: The seminal passage in modern science fiction defining 'Cyberspace'—coined by Gibson as a shared, virtual-reality spatialization of global computer data networks, inspiring the real-world development of the World Wide Web.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 56.
Benedikt, Michael. Cyberspace: First Steps. MIT Press, 1991.

annotations.target_phrase: Lines of light ranged in the non space of the mind, clusters and constellations of data. Like city lights, receding...
annotations.annotation_text: Gibson's lyrical spatialization of digital information as infinite illuminated geometric grids, drawing on cognitive mapping and architectural perspectives of nocturnal urban sprawl.
sources: Gibson, William. Neuromancer. Ace Books, 1984, p. 56.
